what: The claim sentences of the 2026 Riemann-hypothesis story as the pinned sources print them (corpus/riemann, tools/riemann.py) — the release's headline, abstracts, scope note and Lean statements; the paper's theorem, constants and ceiling section; the Lean formalization's README, metadata, definitions and numeric certificate; Anthropic's post; the video's captions — one row per sentence or fragment with a quantity (a few without, for the tiers), each a byte-for-byte substring of its pinned file (a battery check), tagged by who wrote it. The corpus the grammar's coverage of the story is measured on (records/riemann-coverage.json): a refusal is the grammar saying so.

rows.text: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including $`\zeta(s)`$, is zero-free in $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
rows.author: OpenAI (the model's manuscript, as the release's index prints its abstract)

rows.text: A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $`\Re s\gt 11/12`$.
rows.author: OpenAI (the model's manuscript, as the release's index prints its abstract)

rows.text: We prove that all finite-order Hecke L-functions over $`\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})`$ and all Dirichlet L-functions are zero-free in the half-plane $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$, with the principal pole at s = 1 allowed.
rows.author: OpenAI (the model's manuscript, as the release's index prints its abstract)

rows.text: In particular, the Riemann zeta function is zero-free in this half-plane, proving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.
rows.author: OpenAI (the model's manuscript, as the release's index prints its abstract)

rows.text: We establish the quasi-Riemann hypothesis by proving that every Dirichlet L-function, including Riemann's zeta function, has no zeros in the half-plane $`\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}\nolimits s\gt 11/12`$.
rows.author: OpenAI (the model's manuscript, as the release's index prints its abstract)

rows.text: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that every real zero $`\beta\in(0,1)`$ of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q ≥ 3 satisfies $`(1-\beta)\log q\ge c`$.
rows.author: OpenAI (the model's manuscript, as the release's index prints its abstract)
